articles.title: 15 Indian-origin men charged in Canada extortion probe; police release photos
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Calgary Police have charged 15 men, primarily Indian nationals, in a violent extortion investigation aimed at the South Asian community, publishing their photographs to gather public assistance.
articles.body: Canadian police have released photographs of 15 men charged over a series of extortion investigations that allegedly targeted members of the city's South Asian community.The Calgary Police Service said 16 people have been charged with a combined total of 56 offences. Authorities said only one of the accused remains in custody, while the others have been released on bail.Calgary police have published images of 15 men facing charges in a probe into alleged violent extortion targeting people in the city’s South Asian community.According to police, most of those charged are Indian nationals of Punjabi origin who were living in Canada on student or work permits. Investigators also said that none of the accused is Canadian citizens.The cases are linked to a broader investigation into alleged extortion schemes involving threats, intimidation and violence. Police have identified 49 extortion-related incidents, including 19 shootings, across the city.Investigators believe some suspects used aliases or false identities, complicating efforts to track their activities and connections.During a press conference, Superintendent Jeff Bell said the public release of the photographs is intended to help police gather information about the accused, their associates and any names they may have used.“These incidents are often co-ordinated and involve networks of individuals,” Bell said. He urged residents to share any information about where the accused spend time, who they associate with and other details that could assist investigators.Bell also raised concerns that most of the accused have been granted bail and are back in the community. He noted that decisions on bail are made by the courts after reviewing submissions from prosecutors and defence lawyers.Police allege criminal groups used shootings at homes and vehicles, along with other threats, to pressure victims into making payments. Investigators say the incidents form part of a pattern that has emerged in several Canadian cities with large South Asian populations.Authorities are continuing to seek information from the public, particularly from members of Calgary's South Asian community, as the investigation moves forward.Among those charged are Ravjot Toor, 20; Germanjeet Singh, 22; Jaskaran Singh, 21; Karanbir Singh, 21; Amandeep Singh, 21; Anurag Sidhu, 21; Ishandeep Singh, 19; Amandeep Mallhi, 39; Sandeep Singh, 32; Daksh Gautam, 25; Akashdeep Singh, 19; Gagandeep Singh, 29; Pardeep Singh, 24; Taranveer Singh, 24; and Gurkaran Dhaliwal, 21.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Rare Cong-BJP unity in Bengal over Bageshwar Baba's Durga Puja meat diktat
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Congress' West Bengal unit on Tuesday lodged a police complaint against Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent “a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress' West Bengal unit on Tuesday lodged a police complaint against Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent “avoid non-veg during Durga Puja” remark, asserting that the call was “intended to create disharmony.”In the complaint submitted to the officer-in-charge of Kolkata’s Bhawanipore police station, the South Kolkata District Congress Committee alleged that Shastri made “derogatory” comments during an event in Howrah on September 5.“We want to apprise you that immediate administrative action needs to be initiated, and an FIR needs to be registered with necessary arrests. His remarks could spark disharmony in society and were against the democratic spirit,” Congress leader Pradip Prasad said in the complaint, according to PTI.The self-styled godman, popularly known as “Bageshwar Baba," had appealed to Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food during the Durga Puja festivities and described those who eat meat on religious occasions as “hypocrites."Congress, BJP on same pageThe Congress’ move put it on the same page as the BJP, West Bengal’s ruling party, in a rare display of unity between the two national rivals.BJP West Bengal chief Samik Bhattacharya had already rejected Shastri’s call, saying that Bengalis would “continue to eat what they have been eating.”“We generally eat ‘luchi’ on Ashtami and goat meat on Navami. We will continue to do that. Nobody can tell the people of West Bengal what they should eat,” Bhattacharya said.“Let me live the way I want to. Bengalis will eat what they have been eating. Can Bengalis not eat fish and meat?” he asked, quoting Swami Vivekananda.While saying that he respected Shastri as a religious figure, Bhattacharya argued that the self-styled godman’s personal views should not dictate what Bengali society should eat.The issue has sparked a wider debate in West Bengal, where fish and meat are closely associated with traditional Bengali cuisine, while religious practices vary across communities and regions.Durga Puja, celebrated with great pomp and fervour in West Bengal, will be held from October 16-20.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UAE leader warned Netanyahu of Hamas attack days before Oct 7, PM dismissed warning: Report
articles.summary: Middle East News: Days before Hamas stormed into Israel on October 7, 2023, UAE president Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed reportedly delivered prime minister Benjamin Netanyah.
articles.body: Days before Hamas stormed into Israel on October 7, 2023, UAE president Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed reportedly delivered prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu a direct warning that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was preparing a major attack. Netanyahu, however, did not share the warning with Israel’s senior security leadership, according to a new investigation report.According to Israeli publication Haaretz, which based its report on the new book, ‘Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment’, MBZ spoke to Netanyahu for 45 minutes from Abu Dhabi, around 10 days before Hamas launched its October 7 attack.Haaretz said the three senior foreign officials were updated on the contents of the 45-minute phone call at the end of September. The account, additionally, draws on interviews with senior Israeli officials, recordings, internal documents and correspondence.A close adviser to bin Zayed, who was aware of the conversation, told Haaretz that the Emirati president had sought to convey the seriousness of the threat.“The emir explained that, in his assessment, Sinwar was preparing for a major event,” the adviser said. “He told Netanyahu that Israel should be ready.”Bin Zayed also urged Netanyahu to address the wider sources of instability, including the economic situation in Gaza and rising tensions in the West Bank.According to the adviser, MBZ was surprised by Netanyahu’s response, as he did not appear alarmed. He told bin Zayed that he believed Hamas was preparing to act in the West Bank and assured him that Israel was ready to respond to any scenario.The Emirati leader later discussed the warning with CIA director William J Burns, according to Haaretz. Bin Zayed reportedly described his concern that ‘something there is about to explode’ and said Netanyahu had focused instead on the West Bank.The information reaching bin Zayed had reportedly originated with Yahya Sinwar. Haaretz said a Fatah figure involved in contacts over a prisoner deal had received repeated warnings from the Hamas leader after negotiations stalled.“Tell the Israelis if they don’t advance, I’m preparing a huge surprise for them,” Sinwar reportedly said in one exchange. “Tell them to expect an earthquake.”In another conversation, he described his plans as “a formidable operation”, according to the report. The Fatah interlocutor subsequently passed the information to a person connected to bin Zayed."The emir hoped that despite his reserved response, Netanyahu would take the message seriously and take action," the adviser says. Instead, Netanyahu chose not to brief the heads of his defense establishment. Israel’s top security chiefs, including the Shin Bet and Mossad heads and the IDF chief of staff, were not informed.Haaretz also reported that Egypt’s intelligence chief, gen. Abbas Kamel, separately warned Netanyahu around the same period about “something unusual, a terrifying operation” that Hamas was preparing.Netanyahu reportedly responded, “In Gaza, we are in the picture, we are in control. Our problem is with the West Bank, and that's where we are also diverting forces.”On October 1, Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar again raised the possibility of taking proactive action against Hamas, including targeting senior figures. Haaretz said Netanyahu did not approve or reject the proposals and did not disclose his reported conversation with bin Zayed.A senior Shin Bet official told Haaretz that knowledge of the warning could have changed how the agency interpreted other intelligence.“If we had known about the warnings, there’s a chance it would have given much greater weight to the initial message that reached us from Sinwar,” the official said.The official added, “Perhaps it would have also clarified what was behind his sudden withdrawal from the de-escalation talks in early September. It’s possible we would have put two and two together and reached a completely different conclusion from the one we arrived at, one that might have altered our entire intelligence picture.”Netanyahu’s office has rejected the central allegation. In a response cited by Times of Israel, the Prime Minister’s Office called the report “a total lie!” and said, “Prime Minister Netanyahu did not speak with the president of the United Arab Emirates during the period in question and received no warning from him.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Man accused of triple murder admits gun charges
articles.summary: A man is in court in South Africa two months after his wife and daughters are found dead in the UK.
articles.body:
A man accused of killing his wife and two daughters in the UK has admitted unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition in South Africa.

Nothabo Zandile Tshuma, 42, and her daughters Natalie, 15, and Nala, five, were found with fatal head injuries in Great Denham, near Bedford, on 7 July.

Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, 45, was arrested in Johannesburg after leaving the UK. South African police said he was found with a gun and ammunition he bought in the country and he has appeared before magistrates in the city for a plea hearing.

The Crown Prosecution Service in England has authorised three murder charges against Tshuma and an extradition hearing is due to take place in South Africa on Thursday.

The defendant is a British citizen of Zimbabwean heritage.

He could face sentencing for the gun offences later.

articles.title: Some veterans to be called up to test UK's resilience for war
articles.summary: An exercise next year on a scale not seen for a "very long time" will test the UK's preparedness, a minister says.
articles.body:
Some veterans will be mobilised as part of a major exercise next year testing the UK's resilience for war.

The government exercise will challenge the Ministry of Defence (MoD) "on a scale that we haven't seen for a very long time" on its reaction in the event of a conflict, armed forces minister Louise Sandher-Jones said.

The drill will involve an as-yet unspecified number of the British military's strategic reserve, which has an estimated 95,000 retired regular and reserve officers.

It forms part of a plan by the MoD for a "real step change" to use the strategic reserve more, following warnings of a workforce retention crisis .

Sandher-Jones is herself part of the strategic reserve, having previously served in the British Army as an intelligence officer before becoming an MP.

"Certainly when I left the Army and found out I was in the strategic reserve, I just filed it away and never thought about it again," she told the House of Lords national resilience committee on Monday.

"We are definitely no longer in that space - the strategic reserve is a real commitment for those who are in it, and they will be exercised as part of our exercise programme next year."

The exercise in 2027 will "go through measures to call out, to use and equip" procedures to mobilise retired troops at scale should it ever be needed, she added.

It comes after the chief of the defence staff, Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton, warned in January there was not an effective system of engaging them.

Earlier this year, ministers raised the age limit for the strategic reserve - which includes the Army, Navy and Royal Air Force - from 55 to 65 and lowered the threshold for them being called into service.

The government is under pressure to raise defence spending to 3% of gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of the decade, up from an estimated 2.4% last year, according to Nato figures.

A major government awareness campaign will also take place in the coming months to make the public more prepared for emergencies.

Briefings have suggested this could include stockpiling tinned food and bottled water in the event of extreme weather and cyber attacks .

Sandher-Jones praised Finland for "showing the way ahead" with Europe's largest civil defence exercise since World War Two, which saw more than 2,000 people take part in an underground sports hall earlier this week.

She also said young people would prove essential to the military's readiness for future threats.

She hinted a new military "gap year" for under-25s, announced in December and now recruiting its first 150 students until March 2027, could be scaled up faster if it proves successful.

She added that the military "has a role in combatting Neets", the official term for the one in eight young people in the UK who are not in education, employment or training, by expanding cadets in schools.

articles.title: Why Harry and Meghan were caught off guard by King Charles’ latest letter
articles.summary: UK News: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan were surprised by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III clarifying that they remain non-working members of the .
articles.body: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan were surprised by a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III clarifying that they remain non-working members of the British royal family and private citizens, their spokesperson said.The letter, authorised by Charles and sent to senior British officials on Monday, made clear that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were no longer working members of the royal family.According to Reuters, a spokesperson for the couple said Harry and Meghan had only been informed shortly before the letter was sent and were surprised by what had occurred.The couple and their two children returned to live in Britain last month, six years after stepping down from royal duties and moving to the United States during a period of strained relations with the royal family.Their return had also come as a surprise to close family members, with Harry's father, the king, being informed only days before the news became public, according to Reuters.King reiterates Harry and Meghan's private statusThe letter said the couple's status, originally agreed with the late Queen Elizabeth in 2020, gave them personal latitude "in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish"."It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. ... The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity," the letter said."In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."The letter was sent by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the royal household, to senior government and military officials, as well as lord lieutenants, who serve as the king's personal representatives around the country."To help avoid doubt or confusion, the King has directed that (this) information be shared," the letter said, according to Reuters.The communication also reiterated that Harry and Meghan would continue to refrain from using their royal titles as they have done since stepping back from official royal duties in 2020.Any charitable work undertaken by them would be carried out in a private capacity.The letter said questions from official and state organisations about courtesies extended to the couple, particularly where public funds may be involved, should be directed to Buckingham Palace.Security decision due after Harry's returnThe question of Harry's publicly funded security remains a separate issue.Since leaving for the United States, Harry has accused the royal family of neglect, the tabloid press of ruining his life and the government of failing to provide automatic police protection that would allow him to return to Britain.A committee responsible for deciding the level of security provided to him at public expense is due to meet this week to determine what protection he and his family should receive following their return.The government panel, known as RAVEC, or the Royal and VIP Executive Committee, is responsible for the decision on whether round-the-clock police protection should be restored.The letter said operational security decisions remained matters for the relevant police agencies.Harry has fought a long-running legal and public battle over the withdrawal of his publicly funded police protection after he and Meghan gave up their royal roles.Couple continue commercial and charitable workSince moving to the United States, Harry and Meghan have continued to attract public attention and have entered into several commercial arrangements.They have struck a number of commercial deals, most notably with streaming company Netflix, while Meghan has launched her lifestyle brand As Ever.The letter from the king said the couple's charitable work would remain a private matter and that their position was that of private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.The clarification comes after their return to Britain, while their formal status within the royal family remains unchanged.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
